headline: Nothing sealed, and the run moved the repository from an unrefutable blocker to a named one. The first draw's BC-10 finding was caused by this lane's OWN module - java_examples.py supplied only java.io and java.util, so three of eight examples were NOT_VERIFIED and could not be rendered - and that is fixed in this iteration with its mutation test. On the fixed extractor the candidate verifies 8 of 8 examples, renders seven of them, passes BC-01 through BC-09, and fails BC-10 on ONE finding whose cause is measured: _normalized() strips a Markdown link's target, so the literal-value rule cannot see that the finding cites the very SUPPORTED link_target fact its quote renders. With that one comparison widened, the verdict is ACCEPT with 0 blocking findings.

proposal_AD.fix: Measure an absence claim against the plan and the fact set rather than against candidate bytes: a claim whose content is an example the plan renders in that section is 'present', and one naming an example whose fact is not SUPPORTED is settled as unsatisfiable and recorded as such.
proposal_AD.alternative_rejected: Matching the upstream heading's text inside the candidate - substring matching on prose (loop-prompt.md section 3), which fails precisely here because two honest documents head the same example differently.
proposal_AD.mutation_test: A finding whose absent claims name examples the plan renders must not block; one naming a SUPPORTED example genuinely absent from the plan must still block.
proposal_AD.standing: This draw's own remainder was removed by the lane-owned fix above, so AD is recorded as a LATENT class, not as this repository's standing blocker.

proposal_AE.title: A repair whose every change is byte-identical is recorded 'repaired', and it costs the finding its one attempt.
proposal_AE.file: src/repository_presenter/components/readme/repair/rounds.py, the repairs.record(defect, 'repaired', ...) that ends an attempt (line 524), with repair_checks in repair/targeted.py the place a check belongs.
proposal_AE.measured_zero_provider_calls: repairs.json's single attempt (F07, S6, additional_examples, misrouted false) returned 10 changes R01-R10 and 10 of 10 have before == after to the byte: five units.<n>.slot values (preview, workflow:example:002, :003, :004, :008) and the five unit texts beside them. outcome 'repaired', re_raised ['F07'], rounds 2, and the run ended 'after one repair attempt the equivalent failure stands'.
proposal_AE.history: The fourth time this lane has recorded the shape and the first in which every change is a no-op: PROPOSAL N (2026-09-06), PROPOSAL Z (2026-09-11), and RERUN9's attached observation (a change whose before occurred in no unit and no rendered byte).
proposal_AE.fix: A change whose before equals its after is not a change: an attempt with no effective change is recorded 'no_change', leaves the finding standing, and does not consume the attempt the fingerprint allows - escalating to the stage that owns the content, as a slot-set conflict already does, is the honest alternative.
proposal_AE.alternative_rejected: Trusting the reply's own changes list, which is what records a no-op as work.
proposal_AE.mutation_test: An attempt whose changes are all before == after must not be recorded 'repaired' and must not exhaust the fingerprint; one with a single real edit keeps today's record.

proposal_AF.title: _normalized() deletes a Markdown link's target, so the literal-value rule can never refute a finding that cites a link_target fact - and one such finding is all that stands between this candidate and ACCEPT.
proposal_AF.file: src/repository_presenter/components/readme/review/independent/review.py: _normalized() (its _LINK.sub(r'\1', ...)) as read by _cited_literal() and therefore by cited_fact_defect() - G4-W17 arrival item 63's own rule.

measured_zero_provider_calls.the_strip: _normalized(quote) is 'code of conduct - the code of conduct outlines expected behavior for contributors and participants in the project's community spaces.' - the link target gone with the link syntax - while _normalized(value) is 'code_of_conduct.md'. The raw quote contains CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md verbatim.
measured_zero_provider_calls.todays_answer: _cited_literal returns None, cited_fact_defect returns None, scope_defect returns None, and F07 - the only blocking finding - blocks.
measured_zero_provider_calls.the_counterfactual: With the cited value also compared against the raw quote, scope_defect returns 'the quote contains the literal value of SUPPORTED fact link_target:023 ... which the finding itself cites as its evidence', F07 folds to advisory, and review_document's own rule (verdict = returned if findings else ACCEPT) makes the verdict ACCEPT with 0 blocking findings and 13 advisories.

proposal_AF.fix: Compare a cited fact's value against the quote's raw text as well as its normalized form (or normalize the value under the same rules that rewrote the quote), so a link_target's value counts as present where the document actually renders it.
proposal_AF.alternative_rejected: Dropping normalization, which item 63's rule needs - a reviewer quotes what it reads, and code spans and typography must still be folded away.
proposal_AF.second_alternative_rejected: Exempting the documentation_resources section, which would hide every other finding there.
proposal_AF.mutation_test: A presentation finding citing a SUPPORTED link_target whose value the quote renders inside link syntax must be recorded a reviewer-scope defect; one citing a fact the quote does not carry must still stand.
